requirements.note: Newest first. Each row shows the sender, subject, a two-line preview and the date (or the time for today's messages). Unread rows get an orange dot.
Swiping left offers Flag and Archive, and swiping right offers Read/Unread; both work. Archived messages appear on the Archive tab, where a swipe offers 'Inbox' to move them back.
Each row has a flag button, and Flag is also in the swipe actions, the long-press menu and the message screen. The All / Unread / Flagged chips filter correctly.
Tapping a row pushes a message screen. Opening it marks it read and the count drops by one. The screen has flag, archive and 'Mark as unread' buttons.
Pull to refresh adds two new unread messages at the top, stamped with the current time.
The unread count shows under the title and as a badge on the Inbox tab. It updates on read, unread and refresh.
After a relaunch, read, flagged and archived states and the refreshed messages are all still there.

bugs: The Archive screen says '1 messages' (wrong plural).
The swipe-action buttons don't appear in the accessibility tree, so VoiceOver users can only reach those actions through other controls.
tells: Custom beige/terracotta theme everywhere instead of system backgrounds and tint.
Filters are custom pill chips, not a system segmented control or menu.
Swipe actions are separate circles with captions underneath, not iOS's full-height swipe-action buttons.
The header (unread count, message count and chips) stays pinned when scrolling and takes about a third of the screen. Rows slide under it with a hard edge.
'ON MY IPHONE' caption in the top-left of the navigation bar.
The message screen has an initials avatar, a 'To: You' line and a 'Mark as unread' text pill, which looks more like a web app than Mail.
The back button has no 'Inbox' label, and the title is the generic 'Message'.
A.scroll: Slow drags and flings are smooth: no blank rows, rows don't pop in, and the large title collapses properly. Scroll position is kept after opening a message and coming back. The pinned header leaves a short visible list.

requirements.note: Newest first. Each row shows the sender, subject, a two-line preview and a relative date (time / weekday / M/D/YY), with a blue unread dot, a flag mark and a disclosure chevron, much like Mail.
Swiping left archives; swiping right toggles read/unread. The Archive screen opens from a toolbar button and lists archived messages.

Flagging works from the message screen and the long-press menu, but not from a swipe or from the row itself. The filter menu (All / Unread Only / Flagged Only) works; the active filter only shows in the footer, and the title stays 'Inbox'.
Tapping a row pushes the message, and opening it marks it read. The screen has flag, unread and archive buttons.
Pull to refresh (and a refresh toolbar button) adds two new unread messages at the top.
A footer shows 'N unread · M messages' and stays current.
Read, flagged and archived states and the refreshed messages survive a relaunch.

bugs: When the list scrolls, the collapsed 'Inbox' title sits left-aligned on top of the list content and overlaps the rows passing under it.
There is a 'Refresh mail' button on the Archive screen too, which makes little sense there.
tells: Swipe actions are circular buttons with the swiped row turning into a rounded grey card, not iOS's full-height swipe-action buttons.
The inline titles ('Message' on the message screen, and 'Inbox' when collapsed) sit left-aligned beside the back button instead of centred.
The unread count lives in a grey bar fixed above a bottom search field, which isn't how Mail lays it out. At the largest text size this bar takes about two lines of the screen.
At the largest text size the unread dot and flag line up with the preview instead of the sender.
No flag swipe action, although Mail has one.
B.scroll: Smooth when dragged slowly and when flung: no blank or popping rows, with a scroll-edge blur under the bar. Position is kept after visiting a message. The collapsed title overlapping the content is the one jarring moment.

why: Both apps do everything the spec asks and keep state across relaunches. A is the more complete and carefully finished app, but it is skinned with a custom theme, chips, a capsule tab bar and a pinned header that does not look like iOS. B uses system menus, a system-looking list with a blue dot and chevrons, and Mail-like dates, so it is closer to a hand-built iPhone mail app, despite its collapsed-title overlap and its flag being only in the message screen and the long-press menu.
